title: I built and shipped a free game to Steam about Orange cat eating up everything
author: acem13
selftext:
To built it I used a standart Claude license, and had to wait a lot for 5 hour resets :D but now the game is done, it is a very simple small project and is available to everyone for FREE to play so you can check out what cool things you can build with AI. Of course a lot of testing was done to perfect the game, you can't just one shot good game. 

Game was fully built with Claude and Three.js even graphics and even this trailer.

Orange Braincell on Steam - [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5375400/Orange\_Braincell/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5375400/Orange_Braincell/)

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
People here will ask how: "even graphics and even this trailer" doesn't say how Claude made them. Add one prompt and one thing testing caught that Claude got wrong, so "you can't just one shot good game" becomes a workflow others can copy.

  
For a wider audience, r/SoloDevelopment says: "Sharing your project is fine if you add context or insights." "Solo devs manage their entire project alone—no teams, just individual effort." "Using assets, outsourcing, or working with publishers is fine, but the core development should be solo." "Anyone can participate, but posts promoting non-solo projects may be removed." "Game Showcases must be made by Solo Developers" "Don't overpost your content." "Choose your best work and share 2 times per week to give people a chance to digest what you're sharing." "Repetitive or uninformative spam content may be removed."

  
How did Claude make the trailer?
